blocks.text: RNA is usually single-stranded, unlike DNA, but the chain can fold back on itself to form helical loops. A ribonucleotide chain contains ribose, four nitrogenous bases (A, U, G and C) and phosphate groups. There are three major types of RNA in cells:

blocks.alt: Left: one RNA strand made of nucleotides; each has a phosphate group, the sugar ribose and one of the bases A, U, G or C, with phosphates linking the sugars into a backbone. Right: a strand folded back on itself; bases on the two arms pair, A with U and G with C, to form a short helical stem, and the unpaired bases form a loop at the top. The 5' and 3' ends are at the bottom.
blocks.caption: Structure of RNA: a single strand that can fold back on itself (original diagram after Figure 27.16).
blocks.long_description: RNA differs from DNA in three ways shown here: it is usually a single strand, its sugar is ribose, and it has uracil (U) in place of thymine (T). Where the strand folds back, complementary bases pair and the chain forms helical loops.

items: Messenger RNA (mRNA) carries the genetic blueprint copied from DNA in the nucleus.
Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) helps to make up the ribosome.
Transfer RNA (tRNA) translates the nucleotide sequence of mRNA into the corresponding sequence of amino acids in a protein.
